- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 18d avg), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above prior high.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.0) after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit above zero.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >+10% above 18d avg, adjust down by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For horizon >14 days, model underestimates volatility; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or higher).
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.4 → +0.1 → -0.3), model fails to anticipate; apply 1–2% downward correction after sentiment shift.
